headline: China Open: Alcaraz and Sinner advance to Beijing semifinals as dream clash nears
whyCareReason: Carlos Alcaraz powers past Karen Khachanov and Jannik Sinner battles through Jiri Lehecka to set up a blockbuster semifinal weekend in Beijing.
teaser: Friday at National Tennis Center: Alcaraz sweeps Khachanov 7-5, 6-2; Sinner edges Lehecka 6-2, 7-6(6); Sabalenka rolls past Keys 6-4, 6-3 into the WTA final four.
story:
Why this one matters: Friday's quarterfinal session at the China Open delivered championship-level intensity as the world's top two men pushed toward an irresistible collision.

Carlos Alcaraz produced a masterclass of controlled aggression, dismantling Karen Khachanov 7-5, 6-2 on Diamond Court. The 21-year-old Spaniard struck 26 winners and broke Khachanov four times, sealing his 47th match win of the season in one hour and 36 minutes.

Earlier on center court, defending champion Jannik Sinner displayed trademark poise under pressure. Facing Jiri Lehecka, Sinner cruised through the opening set before saving a set point at 4-6 in the second-set tiebreak to prevail 6-2, 7-6(6). With Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff also advancing into the WTA semifinals, the tournament heads into a blockbuster weekend.
stakes: Crucial 500 ranking points in the ATP Race to Turin and a potential World No. 1 vs World No. 2 showdown in the final.
rivalryAngle: Sinner and Alcaraz remain on a direct collision course for the Beijing crown, headlining tennis's premier modern rivalry.
